title: Religions of the World, Large and Small
length_note: 17 classes, about 8 hours in total. Class 1 sets the ground rules. Classes 2 to 5 cover the traditions that began in South Asia. Classes 6 to 10 cover the Abrahamic traditions and their neighbours in West Asia. Classes 11 and 12 cover East Asia. Classes 13 to 15 cover Indigenous and traditional religions, which get three classes so they are not squeezed into an afterthought. Class 16 covers newer movements and non-religious worldviews. Class 17 pulls the course together. Each class is 20 to 35 minutes, so a learner can finish it in one sitting, or in short pieces with breaks, without getting tired. The largest and most varied traditions (Christianity, Hinduism, Buddhism, Islam, Judaism) get the longest classes. Smaller traditions are grouped only where they share a region or history, so each one still gets real attention. Every class describes each tradition as its own followers and scholars do, covering beliefs, practices, history, holidays and where it is practised today. No class ranks religions or says which is true. Every class needs sourced research, including numbers and dates, before the lesson is written.

classes.title: How to Learn About Religions Respectfully
classes.goal: Explain the difference between describing a belief and endorsing it. Use the course's basic vocabulary. Know the five questions asked about every tradition: beliefs, practices, history, holidays, where practised today.
topics: Describing, not judging: how this course works
Insider and outsider views
Words we will use: belief, practice, scripture, ritual, community, denomination
Why size does not equal importance
Why there is no ranking and no verdict on truth
How religious calendars differ from each other

classes.title: Hinduism
classes.goal: Describe the main ideas, texts, practices and festivals of Hinduism. Explain why Hindus themselves describe it as diverse, and say where it is practised today.
topics: Origins and history as Hindus and scholars describe them
Key ideas: dharma, karma, rebirth, liberation
Texts such as the Vedas and the Bhagavad Gita
Many paths and many ways of understanding the divine
Worship at home and in temples, pilgrimage
Festivals such as Diwali and Holi
Where Hindus live today

classes.title: Jainism
classes.goal: Describe Jain beliefs and practices, especially non-violence. Name key Jain festivals and say where Jains live today.
topics: History and the teachers called Tirthankaras
Non-violence (ahimsa) and its everyday forms
Karma, the soul and liberation
Main traditions within Jainism
Fasting, temples and festivals such as Paryushana
Where Jains live today

classes.title: Buddhism
classes.goal: Describe the Buddha's life as Buddhists tell it and the core teachings. Tell apart the main Buddhist traditions and say where each is practised.
topics: The life of the Buddha
The Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path
Main traditions: Theravada, Mahayana, Vajrayana
Meditation, monastic life and lay practice
Festivals such as Vesak
Where Buddhists live today

classes.title: Sikhism
classes.goal: Describe the Sikh Gurus, core beliefs, the Guru Granth Sahib, and Sikh practices such as the langar. Say where Sikhs live today.
topics: The ten Gurus and the founding of Sikhism
Core beliefs: one God, equality, service
The Guru Granth Sahib
The gurdwara and the langar (community kitchen)
The Khalsa and the Five Ks
Festivals such as Vaisakhi
Where Sikhs live today

classes.title: Judaism
classes.goal: Describe the main beliefs, texts, practices and festivals of Judaism. Explain the main Jewish movements and say where Jews live today.
topics: History as Jewish tradition and historians describe it
Torah, Talmud and the role of study
Shabbat and the Jewish calendar
Festivals such as Passover, Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur
Movements: Orthodox, Conservative, Reform and others
Jewish communities around the world today

classes.title: Christianity
classes.goal: Describe the central beliefs and practices shared by many Christians. Name the major branches and how they differ. Say where Christians live today.
topics: The life and teaching of Jesus as Christians understand them
The Bible and its use
Branches: Catholic, Orthodox, Protestant, and others
Worship, sacraments and prayer
Festivals such as Christmas and Easter, and how calendars differ
Where Christians live today

classes.title: Islam
classes.goal: Describe the beliefs, the Five Pillars and the main branches of Islam. Name key festivals and say where Muslims live today.
topics: The life of the Prophet Muhammad as Muslims tell it
The Quran and the Hadith
The Five Pillars
Sunni and Shia Islam, and Sufism
Ramadan, Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha
Where Muslims live today

classes.title: Zoroastrianism and the Baháʼí Faith
classes.goal: Describe the beliefs, practices and festivals of these two traditions of Iranian origin. Say where followers live today.
topics: Zoroastrianism: Zarathustra, the Avesta, fire temples
Zoroastrian festivals such as Nowruz, and the Parsi communities
The Baháʼí Faith: its history and founders
Baháʼí teachings on the unity of humanity
Baháʼí practices, calendar and holy days
Where followers of each live today

classes.title: Smaller Faiths of West Asia: Yazidis, Druze, Mandaeans and Samaritans
classes.goal: Describe the main beliefs, practices and history of each of these four communities as they describe themselves. Say where each lives today.
topics: Yazidi beliefs, sacred sites and festivals
Druze beliefs and community life
Mandaean teachings and the practice of baptism
Samaritan history, scripture and Passover practice
Why these communities are small, and how they keep their traditions
Where each community lives today

classes.title: Chinese Traditions: Confucianism, Daoism and Folk Religion
classes.goal: Describe the main ideas and practices of Confucian, Daoist and Chinese folk traditions. Explain how people often combine them, and say where they are practised today.
topics: Confucius and the emphasis on family and ethics
Daoism: the Dao, key texts and temple practice
Chinese folk religion: ancestors, local deities, festivals
Festivals such as Lunar New Year, Qingming and Mid-Autumn
Why many people do not see these as separate religions
Where these traditions are practised today

classes.title: Shinto and Other Religions of Japan, Korea and Vietnam
classes.goal: Describe Shinto and at least three other religions of this region. Name key practices and festivals and say where they are practised today.
topics: Shinto: kami, shrines and purification
Shinto festivals (matsuri) and New Year visits
Tenrikyo, a religion that began in Japan
Korean shamanic practice (Muism)
Cao Dai in Vietnam
Where these traditions are practised today

classes.title: Traditional Religions of Africa and the African Diaspora
classes.goal: Describe some African traditional religions and the traditions that grew from them in the Americas. Explain a few shared themes without treating Africa as one religion.
topics: Diversity of African religions, such as Yoruba religion
Ideas about a creator, spirits and ancestors
Ritual, music, dance and divination
Diaspora traditions: Santería, Candomblé, Vodou
Festivals and community life
Where these traditions are practised today

classes.title: Indigenous Religions of the Americas and the Arctic
classes.goal: Describe a few Indigenous spiritual traditions of the Americas and the Arctic in their own terms. Explain the importance of land and ceremony, and why practices differ between nations.
topics: Why there is no single Native American religion
Land, story and ceremony
Examples of specific nations' traditions, as described by those nations
Inuit and Sámi spiritual traditions
History of restrictions on practice, and revival
Where these traditions are practised today

classes.title: Indigenous Religions of Australia and the Pacific
classes.goal: Describe Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander spirituality and a few Pacific traditions in their own terms. Explain the roles of story, land and ancestors.
topics: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander spirituality and the Dreaming
Connection to Country and ceremony
Māori beliefs and practices
Other Polynesian, Melanesian and Micronesian traditions
Interaction with Christianity and continuing practice
Where these traditions are practised today

classes.title: Newer Movements and Non-Religious Worldviews
classes.goal: Describe several religious movements that began in the last two centuries or were revived in that time. Explain how humanist and other non-religious worldviews fit in the picture.
topics: Rastafari
Modern Paganism, Wicca and Heathenry
Unitarian Universalism
Humanism, atheism and agnosticism, in the words of those who hold them
People who are spiritual but not religious
Where these groups are found today

classes.title: Putting It Together: Calendars, Sacred Places and Living Side by Side
classes.goal: Compare how different traditions mark time and place, and give examples of people of different faiths living and working together. Show you can talk about any tradition respectfully.
topics: Religious calendars: lunar, solar, and mixed
Holidays in different traditions that fall near each other
Sacred places and pilgrimage
Interfaith cooperation, and the difficulties
Where to learn more: asking followers, reading their own sources
Course review
